The event as it is dated (about 786 AH / 1384) now falls inside his caliphate (785-788 AH), so the detector's finding is gone. One thing is left open and could not be fixed here: the event's own cited page (al-Suyuti p. 761) places the innovation in Sha'ban of 'this year', and the year running in that passage is 791 AH, not 786. If the event is re-dated to 791 AH it falls three years after this caliph's death and this same finding returns as a true contradiction. Re-dating needs the lead sections of the event's Arabic and English prose (both say Sha'ban 786 AH), the Urdu file and a calendar conversion, none of which an adjudicator may touch; it would then call for removing during_reign -> person/al-wathiq-umar-cairo (and reviewing during_reign -> person/al-mustasim-zakariya-cairo) from data/event/muezzin-salat-adhan-786.yaml, which is the founder's decision.

Stands. The relation is right: the one source both records cite, al-Shirazi {cite:tabaqat-fuqaha-abbas-1981 p. 63}, says Abu Ahmad ibn Abi Muslim al-Faradi took inheritance law from Ibn al-Labban. The dates are what is wrong. The student's died 977 and the teacher's born 990 and died 1057 all come from a date-enrichment pass and from no source either record cites; both records' own prose says al-Shirazi gives no death date for either man. The teacher's dates are certainly a wrong side: on the same page his pupil Abu Ahmad is the teacher of Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini, whom the museum records as born 344 AH (955) and died 406 AH (1016), so Ibn al-Labban cannot have been born in 990; his other pupil person/abu-al-husayn-ahmad-ibn-muhammad-al-kazaruni is recorded as born 941. No already-cited source gives a date to put in their place, a source may not be added, and removing a date is the founder's decision. Proposed: remove born 990 and died 1057 from data/person/abu-al-husayn-ibn-al-labban-al-basri.yaml, and review died 977 in data/person/abu-ahmad-ibn-abi-muslim-al-faradi.yaml. For whoever sources it: Shadharat al-Dhahab enters Ibn al-Labban al-Faradi among the deaths of 402 AH, but it is not a source of this record, so no date was written.

The relation pointed at the wrong namesake. al-Safadi (born 696 AH, about 1297) was written as a student of person/ibn-sayyid-al-nas-al-akbar, the grandfather Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ya'muri, who died in Tunis in Rajab 659 AH (1261), 37 years before al-Safadi was born. The relation's cited source, al-Durar al-Kamina ({cite:durar-kamina-jil-1993 2/87}), names 'Ibn Sayyid al-Nas' among al-Safadi's teachers beside Ibn Nubata and Abu Hayyan; the only man of that name alive in al-Safadi's lifetime is the grandson Fath al-Din, who has the record person/ibn-sayyid-al-nas (born in Cairo, died 734 AH / 1334). Retargeted student_of in data/person/al-safadi.yaml from person/ibn-sayyid-al-nas-al-akbar to person/ibn-sayyid-al-nas. No prose linked the elder man, so nothing else changed.

Both successions are true. Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed succeeded Hassan Sheikh Mohamud as president of Somalia on 16 February 2017, and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud succeeded him in turn on 23 May 2022, at the start of his second, non-consecutive term. Each record says so in its own summary and prose (each man succeeded the other once) and cites the two Wikipedia articles for its edge; Hassan's record also explains that no edge is written for his first accession in 2012.

Stands; the two records follow different reports of a death year the sources themselves dispute, and neither misquotes its source. The question reports its cited editor: the editor of Kitab al-Sunna ({cite:sunna-abdullah-ahmad-hamdan-1441 p. 92}) gives Husayn al-Karabisi's death as 248 AH, and the prose attributes the statement to him. The person's record follows al-Shirazi ({cite:tabaqat-fuqaha-abbas-1981}), who says he died in 245 AH 'and it is said 248'; it stores 245 in the field, marks the date status: debated, and names 248 as the second report in the date's note and in its prose. There is no wrong side to correct: 245 and 248 AH are both transmitted, and each record says which authority it is following.

The parenthesis gives the caliphate, not the life span. The prose reads 'the caliph al-Mu'tadid billah (279-289 AH)': al-Mu'tadid reigned from 279 to 289 AH, which his own record confirms (story_roles: ruler 892-902 CE). His record's born 857 and died 902 (289 AH) do not conflict with it; the detector read a reign span written after a ruler's name as a life span.
